statement: The Ottonian emperors (Otto I, II, III, Henry II) and the papacy developed a cooperative model in which the emperor protected and reformed the papacy while the pope consecrated the emperor and supported imperial ecclesiastical policy. Otto I deposed corrupt popes (John XII, Leo VIII) and appointed replacements; Pope Sylvester II (Gerbert of Aurillac, elected with Otto III's support) was the most intellectually distinguished pope of the 10th century. The system worked because both sides benefited from cooperation; it broke down under the reforming popes of the mid-11th century who rejected imperial control of papal appointments.
